title: Fuel
content: A fuel is a substance that releases sufficient energy to do work as it undergoes a chemical change.
e: Fuel is defined as follows. A fuel is a substance that releases sufficient energy to do work as it undergoes a chemical change. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning.

title: Hydrocarbon
content: Hydrocarbon is any of a class of organic chemical compounds composed only of the elements carbon (C) and hydrogen (H).
e: Hydrocarbon is any of a class of organic chemical compounds composed only of the elements carbon (C) and hydrogen (H). A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon.

title: Catalytic cracking
content: Catalytic cracking is a process used to split long chain alkanes into shorter alkanes and alkenes in the presence of catalyst under pressure and high temperature.
e: Catalytic cracking is a process used to split long chain alkanes into shorter alkanes and alkenes in the presence of catalyst under pressure and high temperature. Catalytic cracking breaks long hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones.

title: Transesterification
content: Transesterification is the process of exchanging the alkoxy group of an ester compound by another alcohol.
e: Transesterification is the process of exchanging the alkoxy group of an ester compound by another alcohol. Transesterification is used to make biodiesel from oils and an alcohol.

title: Octane rating
content: Octane rating (octane number) is a measure of a fuel's ability to resist 'knock'.
e: Octane rating (octane number) is a measure of a fuel's ability to resist 'knock'. Octane rating tells how well a petrol resists knocking in an engine.
